anchors.1: Candidate does not restate the problem in their own words, or restates it in a way that contradicts the prompt.
anchors.2: Candidate restates the problem but omits a stated constraint or input/output requirement.
anchors.3: Candidate restates the problem correctly, including inputs, outputs, and constraints, without prompting.
anchors.4: Candidate restates the problem correctly and asks at least one clarifying question about an ambiguous constraint.
anchors.5: Candidate restates the problem, asks clarifying questions, and explicitly surfaces an edge case or assumption not stated in the prompt before coding.

anchors.1: Candidate's stated approach would not produce correct output even if implemented perfectly.
anchors.2: Candidate's approach solves the problem but is a brute-force method when a materially better approach exists in the reference solution.
anchors.3: Candidate's approach matches the reference solution's algorithmic strategy.
anchors.4: Candidate's approach matches the reference solution, and candidate names at least one alternative approach they considered and rejected, with a stated reason.
anchors.5: Candidate's approach matches or improves on the reference solution's complexity, and candidate justifies the choice by comparing tradeoffs against at least one rejected alternative.

anchors.1: Candidate does not state a time or space complexity for their approach.
anchors.2: Candidate states a complexity, but it does not match their actual implementation.
anchors.3: Candidate states a time and space complexity that accurately matches their implementation.
anchors.4: Candidate accurately states time and space complexity and explains which part of the code drives each.
anchors.5: Candidate accurately states complexity, explains the driving factors, and identifies how the complexity would change under a stated variation of the input.

anchors.1: Code passes none of the edge-tagged test cases.
anchors.2: Code passes some but not all edge-tagged test cases.
anchors.3: Code passes all edge-tagged test cases in the problem bank.
anchors.4: Code passes all edge-tagged test cases, and candidate verbally names at least one edge case included in the test suite before running it.
anchors.5: Code passes all edge-tagged test cases, and candidate verbally identifies an edge case not present in the test suite.

anchors.1: Code passes none of the core-tagged test cases.
anchors.2: Code passes some but not all core-tagged test cases.
anchors.3: Code passes all core-tagged test cases.
anchors.4: Code passes all core-tagged test cases on the first execution attempt, with no debugging iterations required.
anchors.5: Code passes all core-tagged test cases on the first attempt, and candidate traces through at least one test case by hand before running the code.

anchors.1: Candidate writes code silently with no narration of what they are doing.
anchors.2: Candidate narrates sporadically, with long silent stretches during implementation.
anchors.3: Candidate narrates continuously through problem understanding, approach, and implementation.
anchors.4: Candidate narrates continuously and signals transitions between phases.
anchors.5: Candidate narrates continuously, signals phase transitions, and checks in with the interviewer at natural decision points.
